doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Why band photographs show no music on the stands
summary: Rowe asks about publicity photos without sheet music; Willcox says music was used at Carnegie and the Nice picture was a jam.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You know, all those photos you showed me on the wall and the photos I’ve seen of the Whiteman orchestra and everything, a lot of times there was no music in front of the bands. Was that just for the publicity shooting?
Oh, you mean in the movies?
Well, Spiegle has a whole bunch of photographs on his wall.
Well at Carnegie we had music, but you didn’t see it, it was kind of a dark picture.
Normally you would have music in front of you on those kind of engagements.
Remember in Nice? I showed you the picture in Nice. Of course we were just jammin’ there. But all those famous guys.
